newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa finalises contract with DAG union.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa finalises contract with DAG union.

text.p: German airline Lufthansa AG and the DAG white collar trade union concluded a three-day negotiating session in the wee hours of Thursday morning, agreeing small changes to a contract struck between the airline and the OeTV public sector union in October.
DAG had been negotiating with Lufthansa for five months, but said two weeks ago it would broadly agree to the OeTV deal struck in October with the provision that it must be improved.
DAG won several concessions from Lufthansa for all 50,000 employees, including a more generous profit-sharing payment and extended job protection guarantees.

According to the agreement, union members were also given special terms under which they could terminate the contract starting in September 1997 if they felt Lufthansa was not fulfilling the wage deal agreement.
DAG also won an additional 100 marks for cash profit-sharing payments in 1996 and 1997, up from 500 marks under the deal first struck with the OeTV.
Under the OeTV deal, workers were to receive one-off payments and a 1.7 percent wage rise to the end of 1998.
